name: Derived Type Field Access
description: Nested struct field access through fir.field_index + fir.coordinate_of chains; component offset arithmetic in LLVM IR GEP
source:
subroutine advance_particle(p, dt)
  type(Particle), intent(inout) :: p
  real,           intent(in)    :: dt

  p%position%x = p%position%x + p%velocity%x * dt
  p%position%y = p%position%y + p%velocity%y * dt
  p%position%z = p%position%z + p%velocity%z * dt

end subroutine advance_particle

; ModuleID = '05_derived_type.f90'
; Particle layout: { Vec3 position[0..11], Vec3 velocity[12..23], f32 mass[24], i32 id[28] }
; Vec3 layout: { f32 x[0], f32 y[4], f32 z[8] }

%Particle = type { %Vec3, %Vec3, float, i32 }
%Vec3 = type { float, float, float }

define void @_QPadvance_particle(
    ptr nocapture %0,           ; p (Particle*)
    ptr nocapture readonly %1   ; dt
) #0 !dbg !5 {
entry:
  %dt = load float, ptr %1, align 4, !dbg !10

  ; p%position%x: GEP into struct field 0 (position), then field 0 (x)
  %px_ptr = getelementptr inbounds %Particle, ptr %0, i64 0, i32 0, i32 0, !dbg !11
  %px_val = load float, ptr %px_ptr, align 4, !dbg !11

  ; p%velocity%x: GEP into struct field 1 (velocity), then field 0 (x)
  %vx_ptr = getelementptr inbounds %Particle, ptr %0, i64 0, i32 1, i32 0, !dbg !11
  %vx_val = load float, ptr %vx_ptr, align 4, !dbg !11

  ; p%position%x += p%velocity%x * dt
  %prod   = fmul contract float %vx_val, %dt, !dbg !11
  %new_px = fadd contract float %px_val, %prod, !dbg !11
  store float %new_px, ptr %px_ptr, align 4, !dbg !11

  ; p%position%y: GEP (0, 0, 1)
  %py_ptr = getelementptr inbounds %Particle, ptr %0, i64 0, i32 0, i32 1, !dbg !12
  %py_val = load float, ptr %py_ptr, align 4, !dbg !12
  %vy_ptr = getelementptr inbounds %Particle, ptr %0, i64 0, i32 1, i32 1, !dbg !12
  %vy_val = load float, ptr %vy_ptr, align 4, !dbg !12
  %prod_y = fmul contract float %vy_val, %dt, !dbg !12
  %new_py = fadd contract float %py_val, %prod_y, !dbg !12
  store float %new_py, ptr %py_ptr, align 4, !dbg !12

  ; p%position%z: GEP (0, 0, 2)
  %pz_ptr = getelementptr inbounds %Particle, ptr %0, i64 0, i32 0, i32 2, !dbg !13
  %pz_val = load float, ptr %pz_ptr, align 4, !dbg !13
  %vz_ptr = getelementptr inbounds %Particle, ptr %0, i64 0, i32 1, i32 2, !dbg !13
  %vz_val = load float, ptr %vz_ptr, align 4, !dbg !13
  %prod_z = fmul contract float %vz_val, %dt, !dbg !13
  %new_pz = fadd contract float %pz_val, %prod_z, !dbg !13
  store float %new_pz, ptr %pz_ptr, align 4, !dbg !13

  ret void, !dbg !14
}

correlations.lowering_notes: Each `%component` access in Fortran generates a chain of fir.field_index + fir.coordinate_of in FIR. fir.field_index is a pure compile-time operation that produces a !fir.field token encoding the struct member offset. fir.coordinate_of then applies it to compute the member's address. In LLVM IR this collapses to a multi-index GEP: getelementptr %Particle, %ptr, 0, <field_idx>, <sub_field_idx>. All offsets are constants known at compile time, so no runtime arithmetic is needed.

lowering_patterns.description: Fortran `a%b%c` generates fir.field_index tokens for each level and fir.coordinate_of to build pointer chains, which LLVM collapses to a single multi-index GEP with all offsets as compile-time constants
